title: Always on top will break app's window ContextMenu xaml style
author: hoshiizumiya
summary: Always On Top's system-menu integration assumes a fixed menu structure and can remove or corrupt custom entries in PuTTY, RDP, and WinUI applications even when those windows are excluded from pinning.
next_action: Approve a design that preserves arbitrary application-owned system-menu entries.

confidence.rationale: A maintainer identified the structural assumption and several unrelated applications reproduce the same menu corruption.

judgment.rationale: A PowerToys maintainer identified a hard-coded system-menu structural assumption, and multiple applications lose custom title-bar menu items whenever Always On Top is enabled. The cross-application reproduction supports a PowerToys-owned fix.
evidence: A maintainer states that a hard-coded menu-item-count assumption is triggered when the system menu is extended.
PuTTY, mstsc/RDP, and a WinUI 3 application lose or corrupt custom system-menu entries while Always On Top is enabled.
Excluding PuTTY from pinning and disabling only the title-bar menu option do not consistently prevent the corruption.
The issue is assigned to a PowerToys maintainer.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve a design that preserves arbitrary application-owned system-menu entries.

fix_assessment.rationale: No existing fix attempt covers the scoped PowerToys-owned path identified by this lightweight judgment.

proposed_fixes.title: Make Always On Top system-menu edits identifier-based and non-destructive
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Always On Top assumes a fixed system-menu item count/order, so applications that extend the menu can have their custom entries removed or restyled incorrectly.
plan: Locate and manage only the command identifier inserted by Always On Top instead of indexing menu positions.
Preserve all application-owned separators, commands, state, and ordering when enabling or disabling the module.
Apply exclusions before any per-window menu mutation and test windows created before and after module activation.
verification: Verify PuTTY, mstsc/RDP, and the supplied WinUI sample retain custom title-bar menu entries with Always On Top enabled.
Verify the PowerToys menu command appears and is removed without changing unrelated menu items.

confidence.rationale: A maintainer identified the structural assumption and several unrelated applications reproduce the same menu corruption.

issue_context.summary: Always On Top's system-menu integration assumes a fixed menu structure and can remove or corrupt custom entries in PuTTY, RDP, and WinUI applications even when those windows are excluded from pinning.
known_information: The problem reproduces with Always On Top enabled, including when the visible menu-item option is disabled.
PuTTY custom entries disappear for newly launched windows.
A maintainer publicly identified a hard-coded structural assumption.
Several related reports were consolidated into this issue.
inferences: The module likely locates or rewrites menu entries by position/count rather than by the command identifier it owns.
Initialization-time menu mutation explains why windows opened before enabling the module can retain their custom entries.
issue_context.analysis: The evidence identifies a specific ownership boundary: PowerToys must add/remove only its own system-menu command and preserve application-defined entries. The issue is ready for a focused design even though an assignee is already investigating.
initial_investigation: Reviewed all live comments, reproductions in PuTTY/RDP/WinUI, current assignment, and consolidated duplicate links.
Found no linked PowerToys pull request that already implements the fix.

actions.label: Approve non-destructive menu design
actions.design_summary: Manage only Always On Top's own system-menu item and preserve application entries
actions.note: Approval starts a separate fork-side design workflow; this lightweight judgment contains no full design and performs no GitHub write.
